prompt: We are a US healthtech SaaS selling to a private hospital in Dubai. Can the hospital's patient data live in our US-hosted cloud? What UAE rules govern this?
assertions: Leads with the decisive rule: the ICT Health Law (Federal Law 2/2019) generally PROHIBITS storing/processing/transferring UAE health data outside the UAE — default answer: patient data cannot live in a US-hosted cloud

States the exception pathway correctly: exceptions require authorization via the relevant health authority and MOHAP (Cabinet Decision 32/2020; Ministerial Resolution 51/2021 covers approved cases such as specified telemedicine) — not fixable by contracts alone
Quantifies exposure: localization violations carry fines of AED 500,000-700,000
Routes to the right authority for a Dubai private hospital (DHA, with MOHAP at federal level) and notes the law prevails over the federal PDPL via the health-data carve-out

Gives the practical architecture answer: in-UAE hosting (or an authorized exception) for patient data, with a split analysis for non-health personal data (federal PDPL readiness posture) — and advises the vendor to verify current authority guidance before promising any exception
